items.text: This Directive lays down common minimum rules concerning certain rights of children who are:
items.heading: Article 1
items.comment:
This Directive has not been transposed into the Spanish legal system yet, although the Law 5/2000, of January 12, regulating the criminal liability of minors, in general, seems to respect most of the minimum standards established in the Directive.


On the other hand, some of the guarantees of the Directive have been incorporated into the Spanish legal system by the Law 3/2018, of June 11, regulating the European Investigation Order, which modifies Law 23/2014, of November 20, on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union. These guarantees refer to children who are subject to European Arrest Warrant.

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. It applies until the final determination of the question whether the suspect or accused person has committed a criminal offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: There is no legal provision that establishes the temporary extension of the rights of the accused minor. However, it is generally understood that certain rights, such as the right to legal assitance or the right to free legal aid, are recognized for minors, as well as for the rest of the accused, in all phases of the procedure, including the appeal phase.

items.text: 2. This Directive applies to children who are requested persons from the time of their arrest in the executing Member State, in accordance with Article 17.
items.comment: Article 50.1 of the Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions refers to the rules provided in the Law 5/2000, of January 12, regulating the criminal liabily of minors to determine the form and requirements with which the detention of a minor must be practiced. For its part, the Article 17 of the Law 5/2000, of January 12, regulating the criminal liability of minors regulates the way in which detention will be practiced and refers, as regards information on the rights of the detainee, to the Criminal Procedural Law.

items.text: 3. With the exception of Article 5, point (b) of Article 8(3), and Article 15, insofar as those provisions refer to a holder of parental responsibility, this Directive, or certain provisions thereof, applies to persons as referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, where such persons were children when they became subject to the proceedings but have subsequently reached the age of 18, and the application of this Directive, or certain provisions thereof, is appropriate in the light of all the circumstances of the case, including the maturity and vulnerability of the person concerned. Member States may decide not to apply this Directive when the person concerned has reached the age of 21.

provisions.textEn: Any person charged with a punishable act may exercise the right of defence, intervening in the proceedings, since its existence is notified, has been subject to detention or any other precautionary measure or has been indicted. To this end, s/he must be informed, without undue delay, of the following rights: d) Right to freely appoint a lawyer

The right of defense shall be exercised without more limitations than those expressly provided in the law from the attribution of the punishable act investigated until the termination of the sentence.


The right of defense includes the legal assistance of a freely appointed lawyer or, failing that, of an ex officio lawyer, with whom the defendant can communicate and meet privately, even before declaring before the police, the prosecutor or the judicial authority, without prejudice to the provisions of article 527 and which shall be present in all his/her deposistions as well as in identity parades, confrontations and reconstruction of the crime scene.

The detainee shall freely appoint a lawyer and if he does not do so, s/he will be assisted by an ex officio lawyer. No authority or agent will make any recommendation on the lawyer to appoint beyond informing of the right.

The authority guarding the detainee shall immediately notify the Bar Association of the name of the lawyer appointed by the detainee to assist him for the purposes of locating and transmitting the professional assignment or, where appropriate, communicating the request for the appointment of an ex officio lawyer.

 

If the detainee has not designated a lawyer, or the chosen one will refuse the assignment or was not found, the Bar Association will immediately proceed to the appointment of an ex officio lawyer.


The designated lawyer will go to the detention center with the utmost speed, always within a maximum period of three hours from the receipt of the order. If within that period it does not appear, the Bar Association will appoint a new ex officio lawyer who must appear as soon as possible and always within the indicated period, without prejudice to the disciplinary responsibility of the non-appearing lawyer

The lawyer's assistance will consist of: a) Request, where appropriate, that the detainee or prisoner be informed of the rights established in section 2 and that the medical examination indicated in letter i) be carried out, if necessary. b) To intervene in the depositions of the detainee, in identity parades and in the reconstruction of the facts in which the detainee participates. The lawyer may request the judge or official who had practiced the diligence in which s/he had intervened, once it was completed, the introduction or addition of the points that s/he deems appropriate, as well as the recording in the record of any incident that took place during your practice.

c) Inform the detainee of the consequences of the denial of consent to the practice of procedures requested. If the detainee objects to the collection of samples by oral smear, in accordance with the provisions of Organic Law 10/2007, of October 8, regulating the police database on identifiers obtained from DNA, the investigating judge, at the request of the Judicial Police or the Prosecutor, may impose the forced execution of such diligence by using the minimum essential coercive measures, which must be proportionate to the circumstances of the case and respectful of the detainee’s dignity. d) Interview with the detainee confidentially, even before a statement is received by the police, the prosecutor or the judicial authority, without prejudice to the provisions of article 527.

items.comment:
There are no specific provisions regarding the right of defense of the minor accused, therefore the regulation contained in the Criminal Procedural Law will be applied (especially articles 118 (1 and 2) and 520 (5 and 6) of the Criminal Procedural Law).

The Criminal Procedural Law is applicable to the juvenile procedure and supplementary in what is not expressly provided for in the Law 5/2000, of January 12, regulating the criminal liability of minors. Therefore, the conclusions regarding the implementation of the Directive 2013/48/EU are transferable here.

provisions.textEn: In relation to a person detained for the reasons expressed in the previous paragraph (offense committed by a person integrated or related to armed gangs or terrorist groups or rebel individuals), the Judge may be requested to decree his/her incommunicado detention, which must be decided in reasoned resolution, within twenty-four hours. Upon request for incommunicado detention, the detainee shall remain incommunicado in any case without prejudice to the right of defense that assists him/her and the provisions of articles 520 and 527, until the Judge decides

The investigating judge may give a reasoned decision on incommunicado detention or imprisonment when any of the following circumstances concur: a) urgent need to avoid serious consequences that could endanger the life, freedom or physical integrity of a person, or b) urgent need for immediate action by the investigating judges to avoid seriously compromising the criminal procedure.

In the cases of article 509, the detainee or prisoner may be deprived of the following rights if the circumstances of the case justify it: a) Appoint his/her own lawyer; b) Communicate with all or any of the persons with whom s/he has the right to do so, except with the judicial authority, the Prosecutor and the Forensic Doctor; c) Meet privately with his/her lawyer; d) Have access, personally or through his/her lawyer, to the proceedings, except to the essential elements to challenge the legality of the detention.
Under no circumstances may minors under the age of sixteen years old be held incommunicado.

items.comment:

provisions.textEn: The Judge competent for the execution, ex officio or at the request of the Prosecutor's Office or the lawyer of the minor, prior to hear them and after the report of the technical team and, where appropriate, of the public entity for the detention of minors, may, at any time, annul the imposed measure, reduce its duration or replace it with another, provided that the modification is in the interest of the minor and the reproach deserved for his/her conduct has been sufficiently expressed.

During the execution of the measures, the Juvenile Judge competent for the execution may, ex officio or at the request of the Prosecutor's Office, the lawyer of the minor or the competent Administration, and after hearing the parties, as well as the technical team and the representation of the Public entity for the detention of minors, annul those measures or replace them with others that are considered more appropriate from those provided for in this Law, for a time equal to or less than the one pending compliance, provided that the new measure could have been imposed initially taking into account the offense committed.

items.heading: Article 12
items.subHeading: Specific treatment in the case of deprivation of liberty

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that children who are detained are held separately from adults, unless it is considered to be in the child's best interests not to do so.

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 5/2000, de 12 de enero, reguladora de la responsabilidad penal de los menores Organic
nationalActs.titleEn: Law 5/2000, of January 12, regulating the criminal responsibility of minors

provisions.textEn: During detention, minors must be kept in adequate and separate units from those used for adults, and will receive the care, protection and social, psychological, medical and physical assistance they require, given their age, sex and individual characteristics.

items.text: 2. Member States shall also ensure that children who are kept in police custody are held separately from adults, unless:

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 5/2000, de 12 de enero, reguladora de la responsabilidad penal de los menores Organic
nationalActs.titleEn: Law 5/2000, of January 12, regulating the criminal responsibility of minors

provisions.comment: This provision applies to the detention of minors, both police detention and judicial detention, and it does not provide for exceptions to the need to keep minors separated from adults.
provisions.textEn: During detention, minors must be kept in adequate and separate units from those used for adults, and will receive the care, protection and social, psychological, medical and physical assistance they require, given their age, sex and individual characteristics.

items.text:
(a)

it is considered to be in the child's best interests not to do so; or

items.text:
(b)

in exceptional circumstances, it is not possible in practice to do so, provided that children are held together with adults in a manner that is compatible with the child's best interests.

items.text: 3. Without prejudice to paragraph 1, when a detained child reaches the age of 18, Member States shall provide for the possibility to continue to hold that person separately from other detained adults where warranted, taking into account the circumstances of the person concerned, provided that this is compatible with the best interests of children who are detained with that person.

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 5/2000, de 12 de enero, reguladora de la responsabilidad penal de los menores Organic

provisions.textEn: When the confinment measures are imposed on those who have reached twenty-one years of age or, having been previously imposed, have not completed their compliance upon reaching such age, the Juvenile Judge, after hearing the Prosecutor, the lawyer of the minor, the technical team and the public entity for the protection or reform of minors, will order their compliance in a penitentiary center in accordance with the general regime provided for in the General Penitentiary Organic Law, unless, exceptionally, s/he understands in consideration of the concurrent circumstances that proceed the use of the measures provided for in articles 13 and 51 of this Law (modification or replacement of measures) or the stay in the center of minors in compliance with such measure when the minor responds to the objectives proposed in the judgment.

items.text: 4. Without prejudice to paragraph 1, and taking into account paragraph 3, children may be detained with young adults, unless this is contrary to the child's best interests.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 5. When children are detained, Member States shall take appropriate measures to:

(a)

ensure and preserve their health and their physical and mental development;

ensure their right to education and training, including where the children have physical, sensory or learning disabilities;

provisions.textEn: The following rights are recognized for minor inmates: (...) b) The right to receive a comprehensive education and training in all areas and to the specific protection provided by the law.

The following rights are recognized for minor inmates: f) The right to free health care, to receive mandatory basic education that corresponds to their age, whatever their situation at the center, and to receive educational or professional training appropriate to their circumstances.

provisions.comment: No references to physical, sensory or learning disabilities
provisions.textEn: The centers for the execution of the custodial measures will be divided into modules appropriate to the age, maturity, needs and social skills of the inmates and will be governed by internal operating regulations whose compliance will be aimed at achieving an orderly coexistence, that allows the execution of the different educational intervention programs and the adequate custody of the interned minors.

items.text:
(c)

ensure the effective and regular exercise of their right to family life;

nationalActs.titleEn: Law 5/2000, of January 12, regulating the criminal responsibility of minors

provisions.textEn: The following rights are recognized for minor inmates: (...) h) The right to communicate freely with their parents, legal representatives, family or other persons, and to enjoy exit-permits in accordance with the provisions of this Law and its development regulations.

items.text:
(d)

ensure access to programmes that foster their development and their reintegration into society; and

(e)

ensure respect for their freedom of religion or belief.

provisions.textEn: All minors deprived of liberty have the right to be respected in their own personality, their ideological and religious freedom and the legitimate rights and interests not affected by the content of the sentence, especially those inherent in the civil minority when applicable.

items.heading: Article 13
items.subHeading: Timely and diligent treatment of cases

items.text: 1. Member States shall take all appropriate measures to ensure that criminal proceedings involving children are treated as a matter of urgency and with due diligence.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 2. Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that children are always treated in a manner which protects their dignity and which is appropriate to their age, maturity and level of understanding, and which takes into account any special needs, including any communication difficulties, that they may have.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.heading: Article 14

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that the privacy of children during criminal proceedings is protected.

provisions.textEn: All minors deprived of liberty have the following rights: (...) c) The right to preserve their dignity and privacy, to be designated by their own name and to have their inmate status strictly reserved against third parties.

items.text: 2. To that end, Member States shall either provide that court hearings involving children are usually held in the absence of the public, or allow courts or judges to decide to hold such hearings in the absence of the public.

items.text: 3. Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that the records referred to in Article 9 are not publicly disseminated.

items.text: 4. Member States shall, while respecting freedom of expression and information, and freedom and pluralism of the media, encourage the media to take self-regulatory measures in order to achieve the objectives set out in this Article.

items.heading: Article 15
items.subHeading: Right of the child to be accompanied by the holder of parental responsibility during the proceedings

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that children have the right to be accompanied by the holder of parental responsibility during court hearings in which they are involved.

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 5/2000, de 12 de enero, reguladora de la responsabilidad penal de los menores Organic
nationalActs.titleEn: Law 5/2000, of January 12, regulating the criminal responsibility of minors

provisions.comment: The last decision falls on the judge
provisions.textEn: The hearing will be held with the assistance of the Prosecutor's Office, the parties to the procedure, the lawyer of the minor, a representative of the technical team that has evacuated the report provided for in article 27 of this Law, and the minor her/himself, who may be accompanied of his/her legal representatives, unless the Judge, after hearing the Prosecutor, the lawyer of the minor and the representative of the technical team, decides otherwise.

items.text: 2. A child shall have the right to be accompanied by another appropriate adult who is nominated by the child and accepted as such by the competent authority where the presence of the holder of parental responsibility accompanying the child during court hearings:

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text:
(a)

would be contrary to the child's best interests;

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

is not possible because, after reasonable efforts have been made, no holder of parental responsibility can be reached or his or her identity is unknown; or

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text:
(c)

would, on the basis of objective and factual circumstances, substantially jeopardise the criminal proceedings.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: Where the child has not nominated another appropriate adult, or where the adult that has been nominated by the child is not acceptable to the competent authority, the competent authority shall, taking into account the child's best interests, designate another person to accompany the child. That person may also be the representative of an authority or of another institution responsible for the protection or welfare of children.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 3. Where the circumstances which led to an application of point (a), (b) or (c) of paragraph 2 cease to exist, the child shall have the right to be accompanied by the holder of parental responsibility during any remaining court hearings.

items.text: 4. items.heading: Article 16
items.subHeading: Right of children to appear in person at, and participate in, their trial

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that children have the right to be present at their trial and shall take all necessary measures to enable them to participate effectively in the trial, including by giving them the opportunity to be heard and to express their views.

nationalActs.titleEn: Organic Law 5/2000, of January 12, regulating the criminal responsibility of minors

provisions.comment: The Law says nothing about the child's right to be heard, but about his/her right to be present at trial that is why it must be complemented with the Organic Law 1/1996, of January 15, on the Legal Protection of Minors, partial modification of the Civil Code and the Civil Procedural Law
provisions.textEn: The hearing will be held with the assistance of the Prosecutor, of the parties involved, of the lawyer of the minor, of one representative of the technical team that has evacuated the report provided for in article 27 of this Law, and of the minor her/himself, who may be accompanied by their legal representatives, unless the Judge, after hearing the aforementioned Prosecutor, lawyer of the minor and representative of the technical team, decides otherwise.

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 1/1996, de 15 de enero, de Protección Jurídica del Menor, de modificación parcial del Código Civil y de la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Civil
nationalActs.titleEn: Organic Law 1/1996, of January 15, on the Legal Protection of Minors, partial modification of the Civil Code and the Civil Procedure Law

provisions.textEn: The minor has the right to be heard without discrimination based on age, disability or any other circumstance, both in the family environment and in any administrative, judicial or mediation procedure in which s/he is affected and that leads to a decision that affects his/her personal sphere, family or social, taking due account his/her opinions, depending on their age and maturity. For this, the minor must receive the information that allows him/her to exercise this right in an understandable language, in accessible formats and adapted to his/her circumstances.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that children who were not present at their trial have the right to a new trial or to another legal remedy, in accordance with, and under the conditions set out in, Directive (EU) 2016/343.

However, since the Organic Law 5/2000, of January 12, regulating the criminal responsibility of minors expressly establishes the need for minors to be present at trial, the Criminal Procedural Law should not be applied

items.text: Member States shall ensure that the rights referred to in Articles 4, 5, 6 and 8, Articles 10 to 15 and Article 18 apply mutatis mutandis, in respect of children who are requested persons, upon their arrest pursuant to European arrest warrant proceedings in the executing Member State.

provisions.textEn: The detention of a requested person through a European Arrest Warrant shall be carried out in the manner and with the requirements and guarantees provided for by the Criminal Procedural Law and the legislation on criminal responsibility of minors.

Within a maximum period of seventy-two hours after his arrest, the detained person requested by an European Arrest Warrant shall be brought to the Central Judge of Instruction of the National High Court. In the case of minors, from the age of fourteen, the period will be reduced to twenty-four hours, in which the minor detained will be made available to the Central Juvenile Court of the National High Court, in accordance with the legislation on criminal liability of minors.

We refer here to what is indicated in relation to the transposition of Directive 2016/1919

items.text: Member States shall ensure that children who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings and children who are requested persons have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of their rights under this Directive.

provisions.textEn: Against the judgment issued by the Juvenile Judge in the procedure regulated in this Law, an appeal may be filed before the corresponding Provincial High Court.

items.heading: Article 20

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that staff of law enforcement authorities and of detention facilities who handle cases involving children, receive specific training to a level appropriate to their contact with children with regard to children's rights, appropriate questioning techniques, child psychology, and communication in a language adapted to the child.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 2. Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Member States, and with due respect for the role of those responsible for the training of judges and prosecutors, Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that judges and prosecutors who deal with criminal proceedings involving children have specific competence in that field, effective access to specific training, or both.
